devices.name: Metonymy
devices.definition: Naming something by a word closely associated with it — cause for effect, container for contents, author for writings.

devices.name: Anthropopatheia
devices.definition: Ascribing to God human feelings, parts, or actions, by way of condescension to us.

occurrences.note: " I, even 1, will utterly forget you, and I will forsake you ": i.e., the false prophets, who would say "the burden of the Lord."

devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

occurrences.note: The Babylonians are called "a nation from eternity": i.e., very ancient

devices.name: Paronomasia (wordplay)
devices.definition: A play on words that sound alike but differ in sense — pun, rhyme, near-repetition.

devices.name: Personification
devices.definition: Giving human traits, action, or speech to something impersonal or abstract.

devices.definition: A peculiar usage of the Hebrew or Greek that does not carry its literal force — an idiom to be rendered by its sense, not word for word.

devices.name: Hyperbole
devices.definition: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally, that drives a point home vividly.

occurrences.note: "The whole city shall flee... they shall go into thickets." Lit., into the clouds; to express the inaccessible places
of Judah's widows. Other comparisons may be seen
"Though Babylon should mount up to heaven "; to express the pride of Babylon

devices.name: Rhetorical question
devices.definition: A question asked for effect, not for an answer — to affirm, deny, or provoke thought.

So verse 17, " Wherefore should this city be laid waste ? " i.e., Do not die. Do not let this city be laid waste. "Why will ye die, O house of Israel?"

devices.name: Gnome (quotation)
devices.definition: A quotation or proverbial maxim woven in — a pithy saying cited for authority or point.

devices.name: Heterosis
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — of tense, number, person, degree, or mood (e.g. a future used for a command).

devices.name: Hypotyposis
devices.definition: Vivid word-painting that sets a scene before the eyes as though present.

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

occurrences.note: " Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots ? "
" What is the chaff (Heb., straw) to the wheat ?"
" In those days they shall say no more, ' The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children's teeth are set on edge.' " This is what they did once say

devices.name: Anaphora
devices.definition: The same word or phrase begins a run of successive clauses, hammering a theme.

devices.name: Hendiadys
devices.definition: One idea expressed by two words joined with “and,” the second really qualifying the first.

occurrences.note: "Execute ye judgment and righteousness": i.e., execute ye judgment, yea — and righteous judgment too
"And do judgment and justice": i e., execute judgment, yes — and righteous judgment too
" Then the word of Jehovah came to Jeremiah after that the king had burned the roll and the words which Baruch wrote ": i.e., the roll, yes — and the roll that contained the words of Jehovah too

devices.name: Irony
devices.definition: Saying the opposite of what is meant, so the real sense is felt through the contrast.

occurrences.note: " What hath my beloved to do in mine house ? " What follows clearly shows what is meant by the Antiphrasis in the word " beloved."
" Go up to Lebanon, and cry; and lift up thy voice in Bashan, and cry from the passages." This is Irony, or Sarcasm, addressed to the family of Jehoiakim, who looked to Egypt for help against the k
" Howl for her (Babylon); take balm for her pain, if so be she may be healed." But the context shows that it was destruction, and not healing, that awaited her. So verse 11

devices.name: Pleonasm
devices.definition: A deliberate redundancy — more words than strictly needed — to underline or solemnise.

occurrences.note: " Cursed be the day wherein I was born: let not the day wherein my mother bare me be blessed."
" Behold, I have sworn by my great name, saith the Lord ": i.e., by myself, by my own majesty, by all that my name implies
"A sound of a cry." Lit., the voice of a cry: i.e., a great clamour

devices.name: Polyptoton
devices.definition: Repetition of the same root word in different inflections (“dying you shall die”).

occurrences.note: "He judged the cause." Lit., He judged the judgment; i.e., righteously judged
" They say still unto them that despise me,"

devices.name: Epizeuxis
devices.definition: Immediate repetition of a word for intense emphasis, with nothing between (“Lord, Lord”).

occurrences.note: " My bowels, my bowels ! " to emphasize the great distress experienced

devices.name: Synonymia
devices.definition: Amassing synonyms — words of like meaning — to enforce and enlarge a point.

devices.name: Amphibologia
devices.definition: A saying deliberately capable of two meanings, both intended.

devices.name: Epanadiplosis
devices.definition: A clause encircled — beginning and ending with the same word.

devices.name: Hendiatris
devices.definition: One idea expressed by three words joined with “and” (“the way, the truth, and the life”).

occurrences.note: " And thou shalt swear, The Lord liveth, in truth, in judgment, and in righteousness ": i.e., thou shalt swear, in truth (i.e., truly, yes — justly and righteously). In swearing by Jehovah in truth

devices.name: Hypocatastasis
devices.definition: Comparison by implication: the thing compared is not named at all, only the image (“Beware the leaven…”).

devices.name: Metaphor
devices.definition: An implied comparison that calls one thing another (“A is B”), without “like” or “as.”

occurrences.note: and is Himself my righteousness, and I am righteous in Him
In verse 4. In death's dark valley "Thou art with me," for thou art Jehovah-sha.m.mah

devices.name: Polysyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions (“and … and …”) piled up to slow the pace and weight every item.

devices.name: Simile
devices.definition: An explicit comparison of two unlike things using “like” or “as.”

occurrences.note: and are now suffering the consequences. (29) The future blessing of Israel will be under the original covenant of grace: as Mother comforteth, so will I comfort

devices.name: Apodioxis
devices.definition: Indignant rejection of an argument or suggestion as abhorrent (“Get behind me, Satan”).

occurrences.note: We have Jeremiah's detestation of Israel's idolatry

devices.name: Climax
devices.definition: A chain in which the end of each step becomes the start of the next, building to a peak.

occurrences.note: Thus the figures Epizeuxis (" I will hear "), Polysyndeton, Climax, and Prosopopoeia are heaped together to express the coming fulness of Israel's blessing

devices.name: Enigma
devices.definition: A dark saying — a truth wrapped in obscure or riddling terms.

occurrences.note: All who know this blessed deliverance which the great Deliverer brings, cry out in the words of

devices.name: Epitrope
devices.definition: Admission or permission — ironically conceding a point (“Fill up the measure of your fathers”).

occurrences.note: " But where are thy gods that thou hast made thee ?" Here, the admission as to these gods is made; but only for the sake of exposing, by Irony, the fact that they were no gods

devices.name: Hypallage
devices.definition: Interchange: a word logically belonging to one term is grammatically attached to another.

occurrences.note: " I knew not that they had devised devices against me, saying. Let us destroy his dish in his food ": i.e., the food in his dish

devices.name: Hyperbaton
devices.definition: Words wrenched out of their natural order, throwing weight onto the displaced word.

occurrences.note: " I will give thy substance and all thy treasures to the spoiler." Here, the verb is emphasized by being put last: "All thy substance and all thy treasures to the spoiler — will I give."

devices.name: Maledictio
devices.definition: An imprecation or pronouncement of woe (“Woe to you…”).

devices.name: Mesarchia
devices.definition: The same word repeated at both the beginning and the middle of successive clauses.

devices.name: Oxymoron / paradox
devices.definition: A pointed pairing of apparently contradictory terms that expresses a deeper truth.

occurrences.note: " He shall be buried with the burial of an ass": /.<'., not buried at all; he shall have an unburied burial!

devices.name: Parable
devices.definition: A continued simile — a narrative laid alongside a truth to teach it by comparison.

devices.name: Parallelism
devices.definition: Successive lines echo one another in structure — saying the same thing twice, or balancing matched clauses.

devices.name: Periphrasis
devices.definition: Circumlocution: a description put in place of the plain name of a thing.

devices.name: Polyonymia
devices.definition: Heaping up several different names or titles for the same person or thing.

occurrences.note: "And the king of Sheshach shall drink after them." Here Sheshach is put for Babylon. The subject is the cup of the fury of the God of Israel (verse 15). Four classes of nations were to drink of it

devices.name: Syllogismus
devices.definition: The conclusion is left unstated, so the hearer is made to draw it — an unspoken inference.

devices.name: Symploce
devices.definition: Anaphora and epistrophe together — clauses that share both their opening and closing words.

devices.name: Tapeinosis
devices.definition: Deliberate understatement — belittling a thing to magnify it, or lessening to increase the effect.

occurrences.note: " The prophets prophesied by Baal, and walked after things that do not profit: " i.e., that led to their ruin. So verse 11
